chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who becomes forgetful in salat (prayer) and forgets the tashahhud. He said: He returns and performs the tashahhud. I said: Should he perform the two sajdahs of forgetfulness? He said: No, in this there are no two sajdahs of forgetfulness.

The correct way to understand this report is that if he remembers before the rukūʿ, then returns and performs the tashahhud, there are no two sajdahs of forgetfulness upon him. Rather, they are only obligatory upon one who does not remember until he has bowed; then he continues in his salat (prayer), gives salām, makes up the tashahhud, and then performs the two sajdahs of forgetfulness, as we have explained.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدَ: the testimony recited in the sitting of salat (prayer)
key_terms.سَجْدَتَيِ السَّهْوِ: the two prostrations performed to remedy forgetfulness in salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَسْهُو: to become forgetful or inattentive during salat (prayer)
key_terms.يَقْضِي: to make up what was missed
key_terms.يَمْضِي: to continue onward in the prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets the first tashahhud in salat (prayer) and remembers after standing or after rukūʿ?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who forgets the first tashahhud in salat (prayer). If he remembers before rukūʿ, he returns and recites it without needing sajdatay al-sahw; if he remembers only after bowing, he completes the prayer, makes up the tashahhud, and then performs the two sajdahs of forgetfulness.
